title: Every customer date and time is printed in New York time, so quotes from franchises outside the Eastern zone carry wrong 'Date'/'Valid until' days and 'EST' signing times
failureScenario: A California franchise. The estimator sends a quote at 9:30 PM Pacific on Nov 19, an evening appointment. The PDF and page say 'Date: November 20, 2026' and the PDF and email say 'Valid until: December 20, 2026', but the link stops working on Dec 19 at 9:30 PM Pacific. A homeowner who opens it on Dec 20, the printed date, is told 'This quote expired on Dec 20, 2026 · 12:30 AM'. That time is Eastern and has no zone label. A customer who signs at 12:15 PM Pacific gets a signed PDF that reads 'November 21, 2026 at 3:15:00 PM EST'. OD11's 'business-zone date' is New York's date for every franchise.
evidence: lib/format.ts:11 `export const BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE = 'America/New_York';` with the comment 'Replace with the franchise's zone once that setting exists'. No setting exists. Production's only zone is followup_quiet_hours.tz = America/New_York, and nothing in the quote code reads it. Reproduction: a script on the release head ran lib/quotes/model quoteValidUntil and lib/format through scripts/accuracy/render-run.mjs. Output: 'sent (Los Angeles): November 19, 2026 at 9:30 PM | PDF "Date:" / page "Issued": November 20, 2026 | link stops (Los Angeles): December 19, 2026 at 9:30 PM | PDF/email "Valid until": December 20, 2026 | expired page says: Dec 20, 2026 · 12:30 AM | signed (Los Angeles): November 21, 2026 at 12:15 PM -> signed PDF "Date:" November 21, 2026 at 3:15:00 PM EST'. The roadmap in docs/accuracy/spec/audit-summary.txt lists 'New York time zone in 11+ places' among the hard-coded one-shop items. The release offers the app to every franchise without a zone setting.
suggestedFix: Add a franchise time-zone setting (app_settings, IANA name, default America/New_York so this franchise is unchanged). Pass it to formatDate/formatDateLong/formatAuditTime/businessDate and to quoteValidUntil/businessYear when a quote is built. Store it in the document for new documents (a new format) so stored quotes keep printing exactly as before (hard rule 1). Show the zone abbreviation on the expired page time as the signed PDF already does.
reproduction: Worktree at 93d9dbc. I ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/vdoc/repro1.ts through scripts/accuracy/render-run.mjs. A quote sent 2026-11-20T05:30Z (Nov 19 at 9:30 PM Pacific) for 30 days gave: PDF 'Date:' November 20, 2026; the link stops Dec 19 at 9:30 PM Pacific; the printed 'Valid until' is December 20, 2026; the expired page (format 2) says 'Dec 20, 2026 · 12:30 AM'. Signing at Nov 21 12:15 PM Pacific gives formatAuditTime 'November 21, 2026 at 3:15:00 PM EST'. lib/format.ts:11 hard-codes BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE = 'America/New_York' and no setting or env var can change it.
fixSpec: lib/format.ts: read the zone from a validated per-deployment value, NEXT_PUBLIC_BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE. Validate it with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` inside a try. Fall back to 'America/New_York' so this franchise is unchanged. Add zone-taking variants: formatDateLong(at, tz?), formatDateTime(at, tz?, { zoneName: true }), formatAuditTime(at, tz?) and businessDate(at, tz?). lib/quotes/model.ts: add an optional `timeZone?: string` to QuoteDocument. buildQuoteDocument writes BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE into it. quoteValidUntil(issuedAt, days, tz = BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE) and businessYear(at, tz). Every format-2 document then prints in the zone it was sent in. A document without the field prints in America/New_York, as now (hard rule 1); no format-2 document exists in production yet. lib/quotes/pdf.tsx (Date, Valid until, signature Date), lib/quotes/email.ts and app/q/[token]/quote-view.ts (longDate, expiredOn) use `doc.timeZone ?? 'America/New_York'`. expiredOn for non-legacy documents appends the short zone name. app/api/quotes/route.ts passes the zone to quoteValidUntil and businessYear. Add .env.example and go-live notes. Tests in lib/quotes/model.test.ts: quoteValidUntil(new Date('2026-11-20T05:30:00Z'), 30, 'America/Los_Angeles').validUntil === '2026-12-19' (fails before: '2026-12-20'). A doc with timeZone 'America/Los_Angeles' and that issuedAt renders a PDF (pdfPages in lib/quotes/quotes-stage.test.ts) containing 'Date: November 19, 2026' (fails before: November 20). sentBefore(doc) and a format-2 doc without timeZone render byte-identical to today. scripts/accuracy hard-rule-1 renders stay identical.

title: The e-sign consent sentence cites 'New York UETA', a law that does not exist
failureScenario: A franchise quotes a property in New York (state 'NY'). The customer checks the box next to 'My electronic signature is the legal equivalent of my handwritten signature (ESIGN Act and New York UETA)'. That exact sentence is frozen into the quote and into quotes.esign_audit.consentText. New York is the one state that never enacted the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act; its e-signature law is the Electronic Signatures and Records Act (State Technology Law art. 3). So every New York customer signs under a citation of a statute that does not exist, and the audit record keeps it.
evidence: lib/quotes/consent.ts esignConsent(): `const law = name ? `ESIGN Act and ${name} UETA` : ...` applied to every entry of STATE_NAMES, NY included, with no exception list. Reproduction on the release head (render-run.mjs script): esignConsent('NY') printed 'I agree to sign this quote electronically. My electronic signature is the legal equivalent of my handwritten signature (ESIGN Act and New York UETA). I accept the option and price I selected above and the terms of this quote.' Scenario s2-ny-consent in rc-doc/new (document.json, page-open.txt) puts this sentence on a new quote built from the production-shaped settings, and probe screenshot rc-doc/probe/open-s2-ny-consent-390.png shows it on the live sign form.
suggestedFix: Map each state code to the name of its own e-signature act instead of '<State> UETA'; for NY use 'New York Electronic Signatures and Records Act'. Alternatively, fall back to the state-neutral sentence for a state with no UETA. Have counsel confirm the per-state wording alongside the open owner question about the neutral sentence. Quotes already sent keep their stored sentence.
reproduction: Same script on 93d9dbc: esignConsent('NY') returns '... (ESIGN Act and New York UETA) ...'. Other states for comparison: IL gives 'Illinois UETA', WA 'Washington UETA', DE 'Delaware UETA', DC 'District of Columbia UETA', PR and null the neutral sentence. lib/quotes/consent.ts esignConsent builds `${name} UETA` for every entry of STATE_NAMES and has no exception.
fixSpec: lib/quotes/consent.ts: add `const OWN_ESIGN_ACT: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { NY: 'the New York Electronic Signatures and Records Act' }`. In esignConsent, take the upper-cased code. If it is in OWN_ESIGN_ACT, law = `ESIGN Act and ${OWN_ESIGN_ACT[code]}`; else keep `ESIGN Act and ${name} UETA`; else the neutral sentence. Leave LEGACY_ESIGN_CONSENT and consentFor untouched; sent quotes keep their stored doc.consent (hard rule 1). Test in lib/quotes/owner-decisions-2.test.ts (OD14 block): esignConsent('NY') contains 'New York Electronic Signatures and Records Act' and not 'New York UETA' (fails before, passes after). esignConsent('ny') gives the same. esignConsent('DE'), ('IL') and ('WA') are unchanged ('Delaware UETA' and so on). esignConsent(null) stays the neutral sentence. Note it in the owner question about consent wording so counsel confirms.

title: Same job, two rebate amounts: the crew's phone and its copied summary say $2,000 while the office says $1,499
failureScenario: The estimator saves the test-in under Assisted with a $1,999 air sealing price. The crew saves the test-out on the job. In the homeowner's house, the crew phone's headline badge reads '40% TIER — $2,000 AIR SEAL REBATE', and Copy summary gives 'Air sealing tier: 40% improvement — rebate $2,000' with no mention of the cap. The office job page for the same readings reads '40% TIER — $1,499 AIR SEAL REBATE (limited by 75% of $1,999)'. The homeowner is told $2,000 and receives $1,499. Only a small line under the tier table ('The rebate shown is the tier amount. The office applies the 75% cost cap.') hints otherwise, and it is not in the copied summary.
evidence: The release e2e asserts both numbers for one job, and both checks passed in my run: tests/e2e/run.mjs:1625 'the crew sees the tier with the saved test-in' === '40% TIER — $2,000 AIR SEAL REBATE', and run.mjs:1690 the office card includes '40% TIER — $1,499 AIR SEAL REBATE'. Screenshots: rc-doc/e2e-shots/17a-blower-door-job.png (crew, $2,000) and 18a-job-blower-door.png (office). lib/blowerdoor/words.ts summaryText adds capNote(e) only when a cost is known, and crews never have one. A render of the worked example from the seeded settings: crew (no price) 'Air sealing tier: 40% improvement — rebate $2,000'; office (price $1,999) 'rebate $1,499 (limited by 75% of $1,999)'.
suggestedFix: When the cost cap cannot be applied on this phone, say so in the badge and the summary: 'up to $2,000 before the 75% cost cap' (or show only the tier reached, owner question k). Better: have blower_door_context() return the capped rebate amount (not the price) for the job, so the crew shows the same figure as the office without seeing the price.
reproduction: Same script: with the seeded Assisted program, test-in 6952@50 and test-out 3325@50.8. With no price (crew phone), headlineWords gives '40% TIER — $2,000 AIR SEAL REBATE' and summaryText gives 'Air sealing tier: 40% improvement — rebate $2,000' with no cap note. With cost 1999 (office): '40% TIER — $1,499 AIR SEAL REBATE' and 'rebate $1,499 (limited by 75% of $1,999)'. The e2e asserts both for one job (tests/e2e/run.mjs:1625 and :1690).
fixSpec: lib/blowerdoor/words.ts. When e.program?.costCapPct != null and e.cost === null and e.rebate has an amount, headlineWords 'tier' gives `${tierPct}% TIER — UP TO ${money(amount)} AIR SEAL REBATE`. summaryText adds `rebate up to ${money(amount)} (before the ${num(costCapPct,2)}% cost cap)` in place of `rebate ${money(amount)}`. With a known cost, keep the current text and capNote. app/jobs/[id]/BlowerDoorCard.tsx then reads 'up to' too when no reading carries a price, which is correct. Tests in lib/blowerdoor/blowerdoor.test.ts: evaluate the Assisted fixture above with no cost; expect the badge 'UP TO $2,000' and the summary 'rebate up to $2,000 (before the 75% cost cap)' (both fail before). With cost '1999', expect '$1,499' and '(limited by 75% of $1,999)', unchanged. A program with costCapPct null and no cost still shows '$2,000' with no 'up to'. Update e2e assertions run.mjs:1397 (refused cents price), :1405 (summary) and :1625 (crew badge) to the new wording.

title: Quote PDF: an option's column header can sit alone at the foot of a page, with its first line on the next page
failureScenario: On a 5-area quote, Best has 13 lines and 8 bullets, so it is not kept together. Page 2 ends with 'Best: Best package', the eight bullets and the 'AREA / WORK / PRICE' header with no rows under it. All of Best's lines start on page 3, so the homeowner turns the page to find what the header belonged to.
evidence: Scenario s6-long (rc-doc/rc-new.ts) rendered with renderQuotePdf on the release head: rc-doc/new/s6-long/pdf-page-2.png shows the Best title bar, bullets and column header at the bottom of page 2. pdf.txt shows 'AREA WORK PRICE' followed by the 'Page 2 of 4' footer, then 'Main house attic ... $3,278' on page 3. In OptionSection the itemHead View has wrap={false} but no minPresenceAhead, and only the title bar has minPresenceAhead={90}.
suggestedFix: Give the items header a minPresenceAhead (about one row, ~30 pt), or wrap header plus first row in one wrap={false} View, so the header always moves with at least one line. Apply this to new documents only; legacy documents must keep their layout (hard rule 1).
reproduction: In my worktree I re-rendered the reviewer's document /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/rc-doc/new/s6-long/document.json with renderQuotePdf (scratchpad/vdoc/render-doc.ts) into scratchpad/vdoc/s6.pdf. pdftotext shows page 2 ending with 'Best: Best package', 8 bullets and 'AREA WORK PRICE', then the 'Page 2 of 4' footer; 'Main house attic over the bedrooms ... $3,278' opens page 3. The page-2 image (scratchpad/vdoc/s6p-2.png) shows the column header with an empty box under it. It happens with two-line rows. My sweep of 405 layouts with one-line rows never left the header alone.
fixSpec: lib/quotes/pdf.tsx OptionSection: only when keepTogether is true (non-legacy) and the option is not kept together, wrap the itemHead and the first item in one `<View wrap={false}>`. Render the remaining items as now. Fix the title-bar orphan in the same change (see missed): wrap the title bar and the first bullet (or the header and first row when there are no bullets) in one `<View wrap={false}>`. minPresenceAhead does nothing on a first child, because react-pdf only breaks when there are previous siblings. Legacy documents (keepTogether false) keep exactly today's element tree. Test in lib/quotes/quotes-stage.test.ts next to the L39 tests: render a fixture shaped like s6-long (5 areas, Best with 13 two-line rows and 8 bullets) and a sweep (Good 2..6 one-line items; Better 4..12 items and 0..8 bullets; Best 13 items and 8 bullets). For every page, strip the fixed footer text from pdfPages() and assert the page does not end with 'AreaWorkPrice' or an option title (fails before, passes after). Assert that pdfPages(renderQuotePdf(sentBefore(doc))) is unchanged from the current output.

title: PDF option title bar left alone at the foot of a page (format-2 documents), despite minPresenceAhead={90} and the code comment 'its title never left alone at the foot of a page'. Reproduction on 93d9dbc: scratchpad/vdoc/repro5.ts builds a format-2 document with Good (2 items, 4 bullets), Better (9 items, 0 bullets) and Best (13 items, 8 bullets), rendered with renderQuotePdf. Page 1 ends with the 'Best: Best package' bar and the body padding under it; all 8 bullets and the rows start on page 2 (image scratchpad/vdoc/shot-2-9-0-1.png). 31 of 405 swept layouts (Good 2..6 items x Better 4..12 items x 0..8 bullets) end a page with the Best title. Cause: in react-pdf, minPresenceAhead only breaks when the node has previous siblings in its parent, and the title bar is the first child of the option View. Fix: together with DOC-5, wrap the title bar and the option's first content (first bullet, or the header and first row) in one wrap={false} View for non-legacy documents. Test: the DOC-5 sweep test also asserts no page ends with an option title.

PDF 'Warranty' and 'Terms' section headings can be orphaned: the heading at the foot of a page, its one-line text on the next. Reproduction: the same sweep with Good 5 items, Better 12 items and 8 bullets puts 'Warranty' at the foot of page 2 and 'Limited lifetime warranty' at the top of page 3. Good 3 items with Better 12 items and 8 bullets does the same with 'Terms'. The section View in lib/quotes/pdf.tsx has no wrap={false} and no minPresenceAhead. Fix for non-legacy documents only: wrap={false} on the Notes, Warranty and Terms section Views when the text is short (or minPresenceAhead on the heading, which works there because it is not the first child of the page). Test: the same sweep asserts no page ends with 'Warranty' or 'Terms'.
A crew member can set the air sealing price through the blower door API, and that moves the rebate the office sees
failureScenario: A crew member is signed in and assigned to the job. Crews are never shown a price; the code comment at lib/blowerdoor/record.ts:192 says 'a crew never sends a price'. The crew member POSTs /api/blower-door/tests with a test_out on that job and airSealingCost set. The route (line 58) passes the value to sync_blower_door_test, which stores r.air_sealing_cost as given (migration lines 283-287) with no role check. jobBlowerDoor() then takes the cost cap from the newest reading that has a price (savedPrice, record.ts:176). That is now the crew's reading, so the office job page shows a different tier rebate: higher, up to the full tier, or lower, down to almost nothing. The office files the rebate paperwork from that figure.
evidence: Kept e2e stack, crew JWT (Carl Crew, Crew A), job 651d6638..., estimator's test-in saved at $1,999 (Assisted program). The crew's GET shows a price of null on every reading. Before: office job page '40% TIER — $1,499 AIR SEAL REBATE | (limited by 75% of $1,999)'. Crew POST with airSealingCost 1000000 -> 200 {"status":"applied"}; stored 'test_out|1000000.00|Carl Crew|crew'; office page now '40% TIER — $2,000 AIR SEAL REBATE | (no cap note)'. Crew POST with airSealingCost 100 -> 200 applied; office page '40% TIER — $75 AIR SEAL REBATE | (limited by 75% of $100)'. Logs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/evidence/crewprice-1.out and crewprice-2.out (probe script: scratchpad/probe/probe.mjs, mode crewprice). None of review A, review B or the blower door build notes lists this.
suggestedFix: In sync_blower_door_test, when has_role('crew'), store air_sealing_cost (and result) as null, or answer 'invalid'. Mirror this in the API route by dropping airSealingCost for profile.role === 'crew'. Optionally have savedPrice() consider only readings recorded by owner, office or estimator. Add a SQL test: crew A's test-out sent with air_sealing_cost 1000000 is applied with air_sealing_cost null. Add an e2e step: after a crafted crew POST, the office card still reads $1,499.
reproduction: Worktree at 93d9dbc. Fresh DB koala_rcv_sec: tests/sql/00_supabase_stub.sql, all migrations, 01_grants.sql, then all 7 tests/sql/*.test.sql (all pass). Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/verify-sec/sec1.sql ran as authenticated with the JWT sub set to crew A (Carl Crew, role crew, lead of the crew on bd.job1). It called sync_blower_door_test with a test_out on bd.job1 carrying {"air_sealing_cost": 1000000}. Result: {"status":"applied"}. Stored row: test_out | air_sealing_cost 1000000.00 | Carl Crew | crew. Before that, the only priced reading was the estimator's test-in at 2400.00. A scratch vitest copy of lib/blowerdoor/record.test.ts used the existing fixtures: estimator test-in under Assisted at $1,999 plus the crew's test-out. With no price on the crew's test-out the office sees '40% TIER — $1,499 AIR SEAL REBATE' ' (limited by 75% of $1,999)'. With air_sealing_cost 1000000 it sees '40% TIER — $2,000 AIR SEAL REBATE' with no cap note. With 100 it sees '40% TIER — $75 AIR SEAL REBATE' ' (limited by 75% of $100)'. The office card (app/jobs/[id]/BlowerDoorCard.tsx) calls jobBlowerDoor on these rows, so it shows exactly these figures. The crew UI never sends a price (BlowerDoorTool.tsx passes includePrice: !crew), but neither the API route nor the SQL function enforces that. I then applied a candidate fix to the function: sync_blower_door_test nulls the price for a crew caller. On a fresh DB all 7 SQL test files still passed, and the same probe stored air_sealing_cost NULL.
fixSpec: 1) supabase/migrations/20261120000001_blower_door.sql, function sync_blower_door_test: right after the can_record_blower_door check and before the line '-- When it was taken, as the phone says (never in the future).', add: `if has_role('crew') then r.air_sealing_cost := null; end if;` with a comment that a crew never sends a price. Leave r.result alone: 50_blower_door.test.sql line 262 asserts that the crew phone's result is kept. 2) Defence in depth in app/api/blower-door/tests/route.ts POST: keep the profile from `const { profile, error } = await authorize(...ROLES)` and send `toRpcTest(profile.role === 'crew' ? { ...test.data, airSealingCost: null } : test.data)`. 3) Test that fails before and passes after: append to tests/sql/50_blower_door.test.sql, after the 'release: readings table privileges' block so no earlier count changes. Steps: set role authenticated; set request.jwt.claim.sub to :'crewa'; call sync_blower_door_test('d5000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1', pg_temp.reading('b5000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1','test_out', current_setting('bd.job1'), null, '{"air_sealing_cost": 1000000}')) and assert status 'applied'; reset role; assert (select air_sealing_cost from blower_door_tests where id='b5000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1') is null, 'a crew cannot set the air sealing price'. Also assert that blower_door_context run as office still gives the estimator's test-in 2400.00. On 93d9dbc this assertion fails (stored 1000000.00). With fix 1 it passes, and so do all 7 SQL files (verified). Optional: an e2e step in tests/e2e/run.mjs where the crew POSTs a crafted airSealingCost and the office card still reads '$1,499 AIR SEAL REBATE' with '(limited by 75% of $1,999)'.

title: The office job page shows the full tier amount as the air sealing rebate ($900) with no cost cap and no warning when no reading carries the air sealing price, although the signed quote's air sealing line is $688 (75% cap = $516)
failureScenario: 1. A signed job (Mona Moneyday, Better, air sealing line $688) has no estimator test-in, so the crew lead takes both readings on the job. 2. The crew's phone says 'The rebate shown is the tier amount. The office applies the 75% cost cap.' 3. The office opens the job page. The card shows '20% TIER — $900 AIR SEAL REBATE' and '20% tier · $900', with nothing about the cap. 4. The program's 75% cost cap on the $688 air sealing work pays at most $516. 5. The office (or the customer it tells) expects $900. capNote() returns '' whenever no reading has a price, so nothing says the cap was not applied.
evidence: scripts/s9.mjs and s18.mjs on the kept stack. The office card text is '20% TIER — $900 AIR SEAL REBATE | 27.1% | 4,800 → 3,500 CFM50 | ... | REDUCTION | 27.1% | 20% tier · $900'. A regex check of the card for /cap|limited by|price/ returned false. DB: blower_door_tests test_in 4800 and test_out 3500, both home_performance with air_sealing_cost NULL. Quote snapshot: Better 'Air sealing of top plates, penetrations and bypasses (1,000 sq ft)' = 688. app_settings blower_door programs[0].cost_cap_pct = 75. min(900, 0.75 x 688) = 516. Crew tool text: 'The rebate shown is the tier amount. The office applies the 75% cost cap.' lib/blowerdoor/words.ts:236 capNote returns '' when e.cost === null. Screenshots: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/release-review/flow/s18-office-blower-door-uncapped.png, .../s9-day-06-office-job-after.png, .../s14-day-crew-tool.png. Related to the open owner question c (where the price should come from), but the defect is that the card presents the uncapped amount as the rebate.
suggestedFix: When no reading carries a price, either cap from the signed quote's air sealing line or show the amount as 'up to $900 before the 75% cost cap (no air sealing price saved)'. Never print the bare tier amount as the rebate. Add an e2e step where the crew takes both readings and the office card mentions the cap.
reproduction: In a worktree of 93d9dbc I wrote a vitest file (copy kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/vflow/flow.test.tsx.txt). It uses the seeded programs from lib/blowerdoor/__fixtures__/settings: home_performance, costCapPct 75, tiers 20%=$900, 30%=$1,300, 40%=$1,800. Test-in 4800 and test-out 3500, both with air_sealing_cost null, go through jobBlowerDoor, which is the function BlowerDoorCard uses. Output: badge '20% TIER — $900 AIR SEAL REBATE', rebate {tierAmount:900, amount:900, cap:null, capped:false}, capNote(e) = '' and cost null. With air_sealing_cost 688 the same readings give '20% TIER — $516 AIR SEAL REBATE' and ' (limited by 75% of $688)'. So with no price, the card's tierFact `${pct}% tier · ${formatMoney(e.rebate.amount)}${capNote(e)}` prints '20% tier · $900' with no mention of the cap. Meanwhile the crew tool (app/field/blower-door/BlowerDoorTool.tsx:504) tells the crew 'The rebate shown is the tier amount. The office applies the 75% cost cap.' The office page has no field where it could apply the cap.
fixSpec:
1. lib/blowerdoor/words.ts: add uncappedNote(e). It returns ` before the ${num(costCapPct,2)}% cost cap (no air sealing price saved)` when all of these hold: e.program?.costCapPct != null, e.cost === null, e.rebate exists and e.tiers?.hit exists. Otherwise it returns ''. In that same case headlineWords' tier badge reads `${tierPct}% TIER — UP TO ${money(amount)} AIR SEAL REBATE`. Use uncappedNote in app/jobs/[id]/BlowerDoorCard.tsx tierFact (after capNote) and in summaryText.
2. Optional (owner question c): pass the signed quote's air sealing item price, already loaded by app/jobs/[id]/page.tsx (signedOption), to jobBlowerDoor as a fallback cost. With that, $688 caps the rebate to $516.
3. Test in lib/blowerdoor/record.test.ts: test_in 4800 and test_out 3500 under home_performance, both air_sealing_cost null. Expect the office words (headlineWords badge and tierFact text) to match /75% cost cap/ and not to read as a bare '$900 AIR SEAL REBATE'. This fails before: the badge is '20% TIER — $900 AIR SEAL REBATE' and capNote is ''. Keep the priced case '(limited by 75% of $688)' at $516.
4. tests/e2e/run.mjs: the crew records both readings on a job with no estimator test-in, and the office card text matches /cost cap/.

Meanwhile the office Estimates list and the estimator's own 'All my estimates' show $3,975 VIEWED and $3,959 SIGNED. OD1 requires the headline everywhere.
evidence: scripts/s11.mjs output: 'after send: ... $3,975 | BETTER | SENT', 'waiting total after send: $3,975', 'server status: viewed', 'after viewed + sync: Otto Offlineday | 1 No Signal Rd · Attic | VIEWED | Quote v1 sent Nov 19 · 12:25 PM', 'waiting total after viewed: none'. The scripts/s7.mjs IndexedDB dump shows {Moneyday, signed, locked, summaryPrice: null} and {Lee, signed, summaryPrice: null}, while the server has better=3959 and better=5060. /estimates as the estimator (s15) shows 'Otto Offlineday ... VIEWED | Price: | $3,975' and 'Mona Moneyday SIGNED $3,959'. Cause: mergeRemote (lib/offline/syncCore.ts:128-140) builds a new LocalEstimate without summaryPrice/summaryTier, which only EstimateEditor's flush sets (EstimateEditor.tsx:150). Screenshots: .../s11-day-01-list-sent.png, .../s11-day-02-list-viewed.png, .../s7-day-signed-row-no-price.png, .../s1-day-01-list.png, .../s4-day-d3-office-list.png.
suggestedFix: In mergeRemote, keep local.summaryPrice/summaryTier when the remote document is the same revision. Otherwise take the headline from the server (the recommended option's stored price, as the office list does) and send it in /api/estimates. Add a test that a status-only change (sent -> viewed -> signed) keeps the row's price and the waiting total.
reproduction: Vitest on 93d9dbc. The phone's LocalEstimate is status sent, rowVersion 3, synced, summaryPrice 3975, summaryTier 'better'. toRow gives price 3975 'Better' and waitingTotal {total:3975,count:1}. mergeRemote(local, {status:'viewed', rowVersion:3, doc}) then gives summaryPrice undefined, toRow price null, priceLabel null, waitingTotal null. The same happens for 'signed'. mergeRemote(undefined, remote) for an estimate the phone pulled gives price null. lib/offline/sync.ts:133-134 and 150-151 store the merged record with db().estimates.put(merged), so the price is gone from IndexedDB. Only EstimateEditor's flush (EstimateEditor.tsx:150) writes summaryPrice, and flush returns early for locked (signed) records. A signed row therefore never gets its price back.
fixSpec:
1. app/api/estimates/route.ts and app/api/estimates/[id]/route.ts: also select what the office list uses: stored options, selected tier, and the signed quote's tier and price. Return `headline: {price, tier} | null`, computed with lib/office/estimates.ts headlinePrice (signed price when signed, else the recommended option per OD1/OD15).
2. lib/sync/protocol.ts RemoteEstimate: add optional `headline`.
3. lib/offline/syncCore.ts mergeRemote: set `summaryPrice: remote.headline?.price ?? local?.summaryPrice ?? null` and the same for `summaryTier`. Without a server headline, carrying the local values over keeps today's phones right.
4. Tests in lib/offline/syncCore.test.ts:
   - 'a status-only change from the server (sent -> viewed -> signed) keeps the row's price': local synced, summaryPrice 3975, tier better. mergeRemote with status viewed, then signed, keeps summaryPrice 3975 and tier better, and toRow(...).price is 3975. For viewed, waitingTotal([row]) is {total:3975,count:1}. This fails before: summaryPrice is undefined, price null, waitingTotal null.
   - 'an estimate pulled from the server shows the server's headline': remote.headline {price:5060, tier:'better'} and no local record give toRow price 5060.

title: While Koala's database is unreachable, every server step waits about 7 s before the app reacts (supabase postgrest-js retries a 503 three times, 1 + 2 + 4 s): /field takes 14 s on the server, the phone's /field 7.2 s, and 'All my estimates' 15.6 s to reach /unreachable
failureScenario: Supabase's gateway answers 503 (the e2e stand-in answers immediately). 1. The estimator reloads the field app: 7.2 s before the phone's copy opens with the banner. 2. Tapping 'All my estimates' in More: 15.6 s of blank waiting before 'Can't reach Koala right now'. 3. Office pages and the blower door shell each take 7.0 s to redirect. 4. The bundle API takes 7.0 s to answer 503. Every step in an outage is far over 3 s, and a real gateway timeout adds to it.
evidence: With the stand-in down (POST /__e2e/rest {"down":true}), curl with the estimator's cookie: '/estimates 307 7.024741s redirect=/unreachable?next=%2Festimates', '/field 307 14.038498s', '/field/blower-door 307 7.026506s', '/api/bundle 503 7.019664s', '/crew 307 7.025404s'. With the database up: '/estimates 200 0.058712s', '/field 200 0.036374s', '/api/bundle 200 0.076123s'. Playwright (s6.mjs): 'reload /field with db down: 7163 ms', 'All my estimates with db down: 15574 ms'. node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js 2.118.0 dist/index.mjs has DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 3, getRetryDelay = 1e3 * 2 ** attempt, RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES = [520, 503]. Screenshots: .../s6-day-06-dbdown-list.png, .../s6-day-08-dbdown-estimates.png.
suggestedFix: Turn off or shorten the PostgREST client's retries for the session and page reads (the client's retry option, or a one-attempt fetch with a short timeout), so a 503 becomes 'unreachable' in under a second. In sw.js, give a shell's network attempt a short timeout before it opens the saved copy. Add an e2e timing check that /field with the database down opens in under 3 s.
reproduction: I built and served 93d9dbc on my own stack (APP 3730, PostgREST 3631, mock 54930, db koala_rcv_flow; the build stopped once at the security notice and the single retry passed) and used curl with the estimator's session cookie. With the database up: /field 200 in 0.19 s, /estimates 0.11 s, /api/bundle 0.12 s, /field/blower-door 0.04 s. After POST /__e2e/rest {"down":true}: /field 307 in 14.05 s (to /unreachable?next=%2Ffield), /estimates 307 in 7.04 s, /api/bundle 503 in 7.02 s, /field/blower-door 307 in 7.04 s. node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js 2.118.0 retries GET/HEAD/OPTIONS on 503/520 and on fetch errors with 1 s, 2 s, then 4 s waits (DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES 3). lib/supabase/server.ts passes no retry option, and public/sw.js has no network timeout.
fixSpec:
1. lib/supabase/server.ts createClient: pass `db: { retry: false }` to createServerClient. supabase-js 2.118 reads settings.db.retry and hands it to PostgrestClient. Do the same in any client that proxy.ts, lib/server/sessionState.ts or lib/server/auth.ts creates for session and page reads. Optionally also pass a global fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(~3000) so a hanging gateway becomes 'unreachable'.
2. public/sw.js: race a shell navigation's network attempt against a ~3 s timeout before opening the saved copy. Bump VERSION to v14 and update lib/offline/serviceWorker.test.ts.
3. Test: in tests/e2e/run.mjs step "Koala's database unreachable is not a sign-out (L36)", with {down:true}, ctx.request.get(BASE+'/field',{maxRedirects:0}) and '/estimates' must answer 307 to /unreachable within 2000 ms, and /api/bundle 503 within 2000 ms. This fails before: 14.0 s, 7.0 s and 7.0 s.

failureScenario: 1. The database is unreachable. 2. The estimator, in the installed app, opens More and taps 'All my estimates'. 3. After 15.6 s they land on 'Can't reach Koala right now ... Try again'. 4. The only control is Try again, which loops back to the same page while Koala is down. There is no tab bar, no 'Open the estimates on this phone', and no back button in a standalone PWA on iOS. 5. They must kill the app to get back to the field app, which works offline.
evidence: s6.mjs on the est-day phone, which has the /field shell saved: 'all my estimates db down: http://localhost:3630/unreachable?next=%2Festimates ... Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/release-review/flow/s6-day-08-dbdown-estimates.png.
suggestedFix: On /unreachable, whatever next= is, offer the phone's saved shell when hasSavedCopy finds one (field app for estimators/owner/office, crew app for crews), or at least a 'Back' control that runs history.back(). Keep the flow-B8 rule of not offering a copy the phone does not have.
reproduction: Vitest on 93d9dbc: phoneAppFor('/estimates') and phoneAppFor('/jobs') both return null. renderToStaticMarkup() contains exactly one control, Try again. UnreachableState does not use the BackButton that the other state pages in components/shell/StatePages.tsx use. app/manifest.ts has display 'standalone' and start_url '/field'. lib/nav.ts:83 links the estimator's More to /estimates ('All my estimates'). The page itself says 'Work in the field or crew app is saved on your phone' but offers no way back to it.

This could be a phoneAppsFor(next) helper in lib/offline/phoneCopy.ts that returns these fallbacks for any next that is not a shell.
2. Tests:
   - lib/offline/phoneCopy.test.ts: '/estimates' and '/jobs' offer the field and crew shells as fallbacks. This fails before: phoneAppFor('/estimates') === null.
   - components/shell test: UnreachableState next='/estimates', with a cache stub that holds '/field', shows 'Open the estimates on this phone'.
   - e2e L36 step: on the estimator phone with the database down, open /estimates. /unreachable offers 'Open the estimates on this phone', and it opens the list.

title: Every date and time is in a hard-coded America/New_York zone, so a franchise outside Eastern time sees wrong clock times on every surface (a Pacific phone at 9:27 AM reads 'Quote v1 sent Nov 19 · 12:25 PM'), and Insights says 'All times on this page are Eastern'
failureScenario: The app is about to go to every Koala Insulation franchise. For one in California, Arizona or Texas: 1. The estimator's list says a quote went out at 12:25 PM when it went out at 9:25 AM local time. 2. Office job times, signed times, the e-sign record and the PDF say EST. 3. 'Today / This week' sections and the quote's 'Valid until' day turn at Eastern midnight. 4. Insights tells the owner the nightly run is 'about 2:15 AM Eastern'. Nothing in the settings can change it.
evidence: scripts/s13.mjs with a Playwright context timezoneId 'America/Los_Angeles': 'phone clock: Nov 19, 2026, 9:27 AM America/Los_Angeles', 'row: Otto Offlineday | 1 No Signal Rd · Attic | VIEWED | Quote v1 sent Nov 19 · 12:25 PM', 'server sent_at: Nov 19 09:25 AM Pacific / 12:25 PM Eastern', 'expires_at: Dec 19 09:25 Pacific; Dec 19 12:25 Eastern; doc validUntil 2026-12-19'. The signed PDF reads 'Date: November 19, 2026 at 12:13:10 PM EST'. lib/format.ts:11 export const BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE = 'America/New_York' has the comment 'Replace with the franchise's zone once that setting exists'. app/admin/learning/page.tsx:422 has 'All times on this page are Eastern.'. Neither release.txt nor final.json lists it as an owner question. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/release-review/flow/s13-pacific-row.png.
suggestedFix: Add a business time zone setting (additive, defaulting to America/New_York so this franchise and stored quotes are unchanged under hard rule 1), read it into lib/format.ts and lib/jobs/dates.ts, and word Insights from it. At minimum, list it as a go-live blocker or owner question for franchises outside Eastern time.
reproduction: Vitest on 93d9dbc run with TZ=America/Los_Angeles: BUSINESS_TIME_ZONE is 'America/New_York', and formatShortDateTime('2026-11-19T17:25:00Z') returns 'Nov 19 · 12:25 PM' (9:25 AM Pacific). lib/format.ts:10-11 carries the comment 'Replace with the franchise's zone once that setting exists'. app/admin/learning/page.tsx:422 says 'All times on this page are Eastern.'. There is no setting for the zone, and neither docs/release/release.txt section 7 nor docs/accuracy/results/final.json raises it.
fixSpec:
1. Add an optional app_settings key 'business_time_zone'. Absent means 'America/New_York'. Validate it against Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') and make it editable on /admin/business (optional, no nag, per OD12). The migration stays additive: nothing is inserted, so this franchise is unchanged.
2. lib/format.ts: read the zone through a getter. The server takes it from settings per request; the phone takes it from /api/bundle.
3. Use the same getter in lib/jobs/dates.ts, lib/learning/nightlyCore.ts and lib/admin/learning.ts. Word Insights (app/admin/learning/page.tsx:422) from it.
4. Hard rule 1: store the zone in new quote documents. A document without one renders in America/New_York, so every sent quote renders byte-identical (rerun the hard-rule-1 render check).
5. Test in lib/format.test.ts: with the setting 'America/Los_Angeles', 2026-11-19T17:25Z reads 'Nov 19 · 9:25 AM'; by default it reads 'Nov 19 · 12:25 PM'. This fails before, since the zone is a constant.
6. At minimum, list it in docs/release/release.txt section 7 as a go-live question for franchises outside Eastern time.

title: Quotes for a New York property cite 'New York UETA', a law New York never adopted, and the owner question about it was dropped from the list the owner is pointed to
failureScenario: A franchise with a New York shop address, or any estimate whose property state is NY, sends a quote. The customer ticks consent and signs under '(ESIGN Act and New York UETA)'. That law does not exist: the project's own quotes.json says 'New York did not adopt UETA'. The quotes stage raised this for the owner. final.json ownerQuestions, which release.txt 7d and report-summary.txt name as the place for the open questions, does not carry it, so the owner of an 'every franchise' release is never asked.
evidence: Probe through scripts/accuracy/run.mjs on 93d9dbc: esignConsent('NY') -> 'I agree to sign this quote electronically. My electronic signature is the legal equivalent of my handwritten signature (ESIGN Act and New York UETA). ...'. docs/accuracy/results/quotes.json ownerQuestions: 'Consent wording (ESIGN Act and <State> UETA): New York did not adopt UETA; have counsel confirm the sentence before a franchise in such a state.' A scan of final.json ownerQuestions: 'New York' False, 'UETA' False. Its only consent question is about the state-neutral sentence. release.txt 7d: 'the accuracy round's open questions (docs/accuracy/results/final.json) still stand.'
suggestedFix: Put the New York question back on the owner list in plain words (e.g. 'Quotes for New York homes cite a law New York doesn't have. Use the general wording instead, or have a lawyer word it?'). Until counsel answers, have esignConsent use the state-neutral sentence for states without UETA (at least NY).
reproduction: Worktree at 93d9dbc, a vitest probe (scratch file, deleted afterwards): esignConsent('NY') returned 'I agree to sign this quote electronically. My electronic signature is the legal equivalent of my handwritten signature (ESIGN Act and New York UETA). I accept ...'. consentState([{key:'shop_address',...}], 'NY') returned 'NY', so the property's state always wins (OD14). docs/accuracy/results/quotes.json ownerQuestions[1] says: 'New York did not adopt UETA; have counsel confirm the sentence before a franchise in such a state.' New York's own law is the Electronic Signatures and Records Act. I scanned final.json's 10 ownerQuestions: 'New York' is absent and 'UETA' is absent. Its only consent question (#5) is about the state-neutral sentence. release.txt 7d points only to build.txt section 6 and final.json, and report-summary.txt:113 points only to final.json. flow.json does mention 'consent wording outside UETA states', but no release document points the owner to flow.json. No test covers NY (grep of lib/quotes/*.test.ts).
fixSpec: (1) Docs, required now. In docs/release/release.txt section 7, add a plain-language question: 'e. Quotes for a New York home say the signature counts under "New York UETA". New York never passed that law; its law is the Electronic Signatures and Records Act. Until you answer, New York quotes keep this wording. Use the general wording, name New York's own law, or have a lawyer word it?' Put the same question in the single owner list from CLAIM-4 (or in final.json ownerQuestions). Check: `grep -c 'New York' docs/release/release.txt` gives 0 before and at least 1 after. (2) Code, only after the owner or counsel answers, because OD14 governs it. In lib/quotes/consent.ts add a set of states without UETA (NY) and use the chosen wording for them in esignConsent. Add a test to lib/quotes/consent.test.ts: `expect(esignConsent('NY')).not.toContain('New York UETA')`, which fails before and passes after, with the existing DE and IL expectations unchanged. Hard rule 1 is untouched, because sent quotes sign under consentFor(doc), the stored sentence.

title: Rollback claim 'Nothing in a sent or signed quote changes either way' is false for quotes the release sends
failureScenario: After go-live the release sends quotes. The owner then rolls back to origin/main c0ae5f1, as section 6 allows. main ignores the quote's stored consent: it always shows and records '(ESIGN Act and Delaware UETA)'. So a release-sent quote for a non-Delaware property, or one with the state-neutral sentence, is signed under different consent text than it was sent with. On every release-sent quote, main also prints the price with cents ('for $5,060.00', 'Price: $5,060.00') in the accept sentence, the signed page, the signed PDF and the signed emails, where the release prints whole dollars (OD4). compat-main only ran main's own e2e on the migrated database; it never rendered a quote sent by the release with main's code.
evidence: I exported the quote my e2e run sent (release code, KN-2026-0001-v1) with scripts/accuracy/quote-docs-export.sql and rendered it with render-stored.ts under 93d9dbc and under a main c0ae5f1 archive (Masthead line removed; main has none). main's page-open-better.txt has 'You are accepting Better: Air Seal + Blown Cellulose for $5,060.00 .', the release's '... for $5,060 .'. email-signed-better.txt: 'Price: $5,060' vs 'Price: $5,060.00'. A copy whose document.consent is esignConsent('PA') (what the send route stores for a PA property) renders 'ESIGN Act and Pennsylvania UETA' on the release and 'ESIGN Act and Delaware UETA' on main. main app/api/public/quotes/[token]/sign/route.ts:107 has 'consentText: ESIGN_CONSENT' and SignForm.tsx:327 '{ESIGN_CONSENT}'. Production's 78 estimates are all state DE (read-only SELECT), so today only the cents would change for this franchise. Renders: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/claim/rcq/{main,release}
